questions.q: Why does Mara write this finding as a brand-new row, R-06, instead of just marking R-03 "Mitigated"?
options: Because the register only allows five rows total

Because R-03 is about the break-glass procedure itself, while R-06 is about the audit process's inability to detect this category of access at all, going forward, for any segment -- a broader risk that outlives the Lesson 16 fix to these 5 accounts
Because Howard Okonjo requires a new row every quarter regardless of findings
Because R-03 was deleted from the register after Lesson 14
questions.explain: R-03 named the break-glass procedure's lack of automatic expiration; R-06 names the audit methodology's structural inability to catch direct assignment -- a distinct, still-relevant risk even after these specific 5 accounts were fixed.

questions.q: What two counts does R-06's description cite as proof of the gap?
options: 9 reported vs. 14 actual
14 reported vs. 19 actual
19 reported vs. 25 actual
5 reported vs. 10 actual
questions.explain: R-06 cites the exact figures from Lessons 11 and 12: the audit reported 14 via group membership, while the actual standing access was 19.

questions.q: What are the two parts of R-06's compensating control?
options: Firing the compliance team and hiring a new one

Requiring every Critical-tier audit to be reconciled against the automation's direct-assignment report before closing, AND making future break-glass grants expire automatically via time-bound PIM/IAM session policies
Deleting the OT-SCADA-Admins group entirely
Running the compliance audit twice a year instead of once
questions.explain: The control addresses both halves of the problem: the audit process itself (mandatory reconciliation against the automation) and the break-glass mechanism (automatic expiration instead of manual revocation).

questions.q: Why do future break-glass grants use time-bound Azure AD PIM eligible assignments and AWS IAM session policies with a capped duration?
options: So they expire automatically instead of depending on a manual 72-hour follow-up ticket that can be, and was, forgotten
So they can only be used once per employee
Because Azure AD PIM is required for all accounts regardless of role
To make the accounts permanently disabled
questions.explain: This closes the exact structural gap R-03 originally flagged -- access that depended on someone remembering to revoke it now expires on its own.

questions.q: Why does R-06's Status stay "Mitigated" rather than being marked "Closed" and removed from the register?
options: Because the fix didn't actually work

Because, consistent with how R-04 was handled in Lesson 10, a working compensating control doesn't make a risk disappear from tracking -- the register keeps showing what's in place and when it's due for review
Because Howard Okonjo has not yet approved the fix
Because risk registers cannot have a "Mitigated" status
questions.explain: The same discipline from R-04 applies here: a mitigated risk stays logged with its control and a review date, so anyone checking later can confirm the control is still working.
